details: Bitcoin briefly surged above $80,000, reaching highs of $80,594, which led to over $300 million in short positions being liquidated across the crypto derivatives market. This event marks the third major short squeeze in recent weeks, indicating renewed capital inflows and aggressive buying activity. The move is also supported by continued net inflows into institutional Bitcoin ETF products.
title: Bitcoin Surges Past $80,000, Triggers $300M+ Short Liquidations

details: The Ethereum network has successfully implemented its "Glamsterdam" upgrade, a significant change that has tripled the blockchain's processing capacity by increasing the block gas limit from 60 million to 200 million. This upgrade aims to reduce transaction costs and mitigate network congestion, benefiting DeFi and NFT activities. The news has already led to a notable rise in ETH's price and trading volume.
title: Ethereum "Glamsterdam" Upgrade Triples Network Processing Capacity

details: A breakthrough agreement on stablecoin provisions within the U.S. Clarity Act, a long-stalled crypto bill, has caused crypto-related stocks such as Circle (CRCL) and Coinbase (COIN) to surge by up to 18%. The revised legislation prohibits yield on stablecoin deposits from traditional banks but permits rewards tied to trading, transactions, or staking. A Senate markup for the bill is anticipated this month.
title: Clarity Act Stablecoin Deal Sparks Surge in Crypto Stocks

details: An analyst highlights that institutional demand for Bitcoin is currently five times greater than the rate at which new Bitcoin is mined. Historically, this supply-demand dynamic has preceded substantial price increases, leading to predictions that Bitcoin could reach $96,000 in the coming weeks. However, some caution is advised due to potential speculative trading.
title: Institutional Bitcoin Demand Five Times Supply, Potential $96K Target

details: World Liberty Financial (WLFI) experienced a 4.42% price increase following the filing of a defamation lawsuit against Tron founder Justin Sun. This legal action has reportedly boosted WLFI's trading volume by 43% and rekindled interest in cryptocurrencies associated with Donald Trump.
title: World Liberty Financial Jumps After Lawsuit Against Justin Sun
